goal: Reduce production ProviderJob fragmentation by planning bounded natural multi-file ownership units without changing the Provider scheduler, transport, supervision, evidence, or delivery authorities.
acceptance_criteria: ProviderJob uses its existing owns list for one or more files and rejects output outside that ownership.

The frozen Local Project Board plan has at most eight jobs, fewer than seven waves, average files per job above one, no unjustified app_part fragments, a valid acyclic ownership graph, and at least two ready independent jobs.
The existing production executor reaches four concurrent workers for four ready jobs, fallback consideration does not reduce concurrency, and only fallback execution applies the local limit.
A failed file in a multi-file job reruns only that stable ownership unit and its graph consumers while unrelated passing units remain reusable.
Legacy single-path jobs and checkpoints remain readable, focused and quick regressions pass, and one bounded live multi-file Qwen Provider validation is recorded.

quality_metrics.measure: single production Provider scheduler and authority preservation
quality_metrics.target: the existing split executor remains the only scheduler and all validation, evidence, packaging, and delivery boundaries remain unchanged
quality_metrics.method: strict rule guard, kernel contract checks, and production executor tests

quality_metrics.target: focused and quick profiles pass with deterministic DAG and repair assertions
quality_metrics.method: frozen planner fixture, fake Provider barrier tests, checkpoint compatibility tests, and quick profile

quality_metrics.target: Local Project Board moves from 16 one-file jobs and seven waves to at most eight natural jobs and fewer than seven waves

prevention: Reuse ProviderJob owns and the existing worker pool instead of creating another schema or scheduler.
Require a concrete fragmentation reason for explicit submodules and avoid browser-JavaScript symbol-count splitting.
assurance: Validate ownership conflicts, cycles, dependency waves, output budgets, and legacy adapters deterministically.
control: Run the focused suite, strict slim rule guard, full quick profile, and one bounded live Provider request.
improvement: Restore paid Qwen access or disable free-tier-only mode before rerunning the live multi-file validation and any full E2E.

interface_expectations: scripts/run_local_pipeline_impl.py remains the sole production ProviderJob executor and worker pool.
scripts/provider_jobs.py remains a pure ProviderJob and PatchSet contract/helper with no scheduling authority.
New graphs use canonical owns/paths lists; legacy path is adapted only while reading older state.
Provider timeout, retry, supervision, evidence, packaging, and delivery policies are unchanged.

feedback: The frozen Local Project Board plan now has six jobs with wave widths [1, 3, 1, 1], four critical waves, average two files per job, and no synthetic app_part JavaScript files.
Focused regression, strict rule guard, and the complete quick profile pass.
The live qwen3.8-max request reached Model Studio but returned HTTP 403 because free quota was exhausted, so live generation remains blocked and full E2E must not run.

worked: A small dependency/output-bound heuristic reduced API round trips while preserving real independent work and affected-unit repair.
did_not_work: The first diagnostic invocation lacked the single-model production routing policy and selected an unavailable gpt-5.5 deployment; the corrected Qwen invocation was then blocked by account quota.
experiments: A production executor barrier demonstrated measured concurrency four at configured parallelism four without a fallback-executed event.
